summary: # CLO Techniques Workshop - Techniques for Making Snap Buttons ## Introduction In this workshop, we will explore the process of creating a custom snap button, referred to as the plate buckle. This technique involves several steps, from modifying the button's properties to simulating the final design. ## Creating the Custom Button First of all, put the plate buckle as a custom button to be added. Select the button at the window of the object, then find the plus sign next to the shape. Click the plus sign to enter the custom button interface. 1. Modify the name to "plate buckle." 2. Open the button OBJ and select the grid. 3. Set the corresponding width and thickness according to the ratio. The axis conversion has been pre-adjusted here, so we do not need to set it specifically. ### Reference Video Regarding the custom button, we also made a video to explain the process step by step. ## Designing the Buckle Head Side Next, let's make a pattern of the buckle head side. 1. Set the width to 45 mm and the height to 1 mm. 2. Select this plate and use the other half of the inner column of the column layer. 3. Combine the particles of these two plates together. 4. Change the width of the column to 5 mm, the thickness of the collision to 1 mm, and the thickness of the curve to 2 mm. Then, place the plate buckle over the 3D window, freeze the top plate, and naturally simulate the bottom plate. After the simulation is complete, the whole assembly is frozen. ## Editing the Plate 1. Copy the plate to the other side. 2. Use the edit tool to select the leftmost side and pull it to the left. Right-click to edit the distance of movement and enter 10 mm. We can use a fixed needle. Select the front end of the back of the plate and select the position where the key shape ring is. It is recommended to add two fixed needles on the ring separately. ## Positioning the Sewing Line Next, we move the sewing line to the position of about half. 1. Select the plate and first remove the frozen hole. 2. Use the positioning ball to pull in the direction of the X-axis to the middle, creating a reunion part in the middle. 3. Move the assembly towards us. After completing this operation, simulate the design. Pull two fixed needles and add a round plate with a diameter of 15 mm. Change the particle diameter of the plate to 5 mm and the thickness of the collision to 1 mm. ### Adding a Sticky Layer Add a sticky layer to the assembly. The type of choice for the bottom ring cannot be stretched. Adjust it to the position close to the ring. Then, use the free sewing tool to sew the plate and the round plate. At this point, you can switch to the texture surface in the 3D window for clearer visibility. ## Finalizing the Design After sewing, simulate the design again and then delete the fixed needle to make the simulation look more natural. 1. If there is unnatural behavior at the opening, set the folding angle to 270 degrees to make it perpendicular to the round plate. 2. If stability issues arise, turn off the folding at this location in the attribute editor. If it is still unstable, delete the sewing line and re-monitor the stability before sewing again. After these adjustments, check the back view. Use a fake sewing needle to fix the round plate to the other side of the plate and perform the sewing. ### Important Notes When fixing, pay attention to the position. The plate facing us means the fixed position should be at the edge of the plate, not near the center. Adjust the position of the fake sewing needle and combine the angle to determine its position. 1. After adjustment, delete the fixed needle of the ring part. 2. Combine the effects of simulation and adjust the position of the fixed needle at the end of the hinge. ## Adding the Buckle Next, add the buckle of the plate buckle to the round plate. 1. Select the buckle and turn off the conflict in the property editor. 2. Adjust the size of the round plate by double-clicking the center point after selecting it. When the top of the outer frame becomes orange, use it as a reference point to quickly adjust the size of the plate. Finally, adjust the suture of the buckle to make the plate buckle look more natural. ### Applying Transparent Fabric Next, apply transparent fabric to the round plate. 1. Select the round plate and apply a new default fabric, reducing the opacity to the lowest. 2. At this point, the round plate should appear transparent. 3. Delete all fixed needles and remove the cold hole on the other side of the buckle. ## Saving the Document Store the design as a clothing document for convenient use next time. 1. Click to add the plate buckle document to your clothing. 2. In the 2D window, place the plate buckle in the blank area. In the 3D window, add it to a spot near the designated area. ### Final Adjustments Demonstrate the placement of the buckle on both the left and right sides, ensuring that the face has been pre-set for sewing. The internal line should be slightly longer than the buckle to facilitate adjustments. 1. After straightening the buckle, if needed, add one more internal line. 2. Set another internal line according to your needs, with two internal lines having a diameter of 2 mm. ## Sewing the Buckle Before sewing, switch to the clothing rendering type and change to the texture surface. 1. Use the free sewing tool to identify the sewing position by following the high blue dots in the 3D window. 2. Set the starting point and click to set the end point. Adjust the length of the sewing line in the left-side window, setting it to 25 mm on the left and 28 mm on the right. ### Ensuring Proper Seam Allowance Switch to the edge sewing line tool and change the view to the bottom for easier adjustments. Maintain an even seam allowance to prevent pulling in the corresponding positions. 1. Simulate the design. If you see any hammering effect on the seam allowance, add a stitch to improve it. 2. Choose the hardest bottom collar, which has no seam allowance. ### Final Fabric Application At this point, if the seam allowance on the side of the buckle appears unbalanced, make necessary adjustments. 1. Copy another plate buckle and repeat the same operation to sew it to the opening position. 2. Apply fabric to the seam allowance board, selecting the window of the lining to do so. 3. Modify the material type to make it shinier and change it to a uniform color. Use the color stripper to absorb the color of the body and apply it to the color board. Next, copy the PBR sticker of the seam allowance fabric and lock the path. Finally, apply the PBR sticker to the OBJ app for fastening and modify the material. You can paste it on the previous path in the next step and directly apply the corresponding PBR sticker to the same path. ## Conclusion You will see that the plate buckle made of real silk fabric has a certain sense of gloss. This concludes the workshop on creating a custom snap button using CLO techniques.
